subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a core global agent dry-run mode as a trusted no-side-effect contract, or keep no-execute previews scoped to per-command dry-runs, approvals, and tool policy?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the requested flag changes the security boundary users rely on before tools, plugins, channels, and client-delegated execution are allowed to run.

options.title: Approve a narrow CLI-first design
options.body: Define dry-run semantics for hooks, runtime tools, client tools, Gateway dispatch, reads, logging, and structured results before accepting an implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader safe workflow modes
options.body: Track this as part of the broader ask/plan/modify direction if maintainers want one unified product model instead of a standalone flag.

options.title: Decline global dry-run for now
options.body: Keep safety previews scoped to existing per-command dry-runs, approvals, sandboxing, and tool allowlists to avoid promising a hard boundary too early.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow CLI-first design
recommendation.body: Define dry-run semantics for hooks, runtime tools, client tools, Gateway dispatch, reads, logging, and structured results before accepting an implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent agent runtime history and VISION/security-product context make this the best available decision owner from the observed history.
